author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.
decisions:
Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.

The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected on the booking form, reached by its own address. The correction changes that visit in place and is held to the booking rules.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction form is opened, then the form carries that visit's current date and description
given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted, then that visit carries the new values and the pet gains no further visit
given a correction that is accepted, when the submission completes, then the owner's record is shown
given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused and the description is named
given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused and the date is named
non_goals: cancelling a booked visit (NG-5, still declined)
a link to the correction form from the owner's record — the owner deferred a visible entry point to a possible follow-up request
changing which pet a visit belongs to
notes: Boundary: NG-5 narrowed to cancellation only; NG-4 (deleting a visit) stands. Recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-21-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md, which supersedes the NG-5 half of the 2026-08-08 non-goal ADR. The ADR index row in docs/adr/README.md is still missing — that file is outside product write scope, so doc-sync or system-design-expert should add it. Reuse of the booking form is the owner's instruction; edge cases 3 and 4 of the Visits section are the narrowest reading of unstated cases (ownership mismatch refused; an already-past visit cannot keep its date). Three open questions recorded in the PRD rather than blocked on, per the intake's standing instruction: the entry point, correcting an already-past visit, and the form still reading as booking. No autofix records to audit.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Correction is the existing nested create-and-edit-in-one-controller flow, already realized for pets. PetController resolves the child through an @ModelAttribute taking an optional child id (PetController.java:75-87), edits it inside the owner aggregate, and saves the owner. VisitController repeats that shape: loadPetWithVisit (VisitController.java:63-81) gains an optional visitId path variable and returns the pet's existing Visit instead of a fresh one. No new package, module, pattern, or dependency. The adjustment that makes this minor rather than covered: Pet exposes no by-identity visit lookup, so it gains one mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer) (Owner.java:117-127), and the shared @ModelAttribute now serves two routes. Basis: direct reads of VisitController, PetController, Owner, Pet, Visit, VisitControllerTests, and pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html; no IDE oracle connected in this run, so the resolution claim rests on file reads rather than symbol resolution. docs/system-design.md Contracts now carries REQ-VISITEDIT-001 on VisitController, Visit, Pet, and OwnerRepository, and the invariant paragraph records in-place correction.
integration_points: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit join VisitController beside the two /visits/new routes
loadPetWithVisit takes @PathVariable(name="visitId", required=false) Integer visitId and serves both route pairs; null means booking, present means correction
Pet gains a by-identity visit lookup; the correction path reaches it as owner.getPet(petId).getVisit(visitId)
the correction handler mutates the resolved Visit and calls owners.save(owner); the JPA cascade from Owner issues an update, matching how PetController.updatePetDetails persists a child edit
pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html is reused unchanged: the form declares method="post" with no action, so it submits to whichever of the two URLs rendered it
docs/adr/README.md index gained the missing 2026-08-21 non-goal ADR row, and the 2026-08-08 row's status now mirrors that ADR's own narrowing note

patterns.description: @ModelAttribute with an optional child id: null yields a new instance, present yields the child resolved from the owner aggregate. The shape the visit model attribute adopts
child edit applied inside the owner aggregate, then owners.save(owner). VisitController needs no copy step, because its model attribute and its @ModelAttribute Owner come from the same load
getPet(Integer) — the by-identity aggregate lookup that Pet's new visit lookup mirrors, including the null-on-absent return
missing owner and missing pet are refused with IllegalArgumentException naming the identifiers. A visit that is not the pet's is refused the same way (PRD Visits edge case 3)

risks.risk: The correction path returns a fresh Visit, or keeps calling pet.addVisit, and the save inserts a second row. This breaks the acceptance criterion that the pet gains no further visit
risks.mitigation: The model attribute returns the instance already held in the loaded owner graph and calls addVisit only on the booking branch. The test asserts the pet's visit count is unchanged and that the saved owner's visit carries the new values

risks.risk: The non-future-date rule is restated inline in the correction handler. architecture-principles.md line 91 freezes the controller-rule deviation: a new rule added to a controller is a fresh violation
risks.mitigation: State the rule once. Both handlers call one shared check that rejects a date not after today with code typeMismatch.visitDate. No second expression of the rule, and no new rule — the same rule reaches a second entry point

risks.risk: A new flash message or heading introduces user-facing text, which REQ-LANG-002 holds to eleven-locale bundle parity
risks.mitigation: Add no message key and no new hard-coded string. The requirement asks only that the owner's record is shown after an accepted correction

risks.risk: Visit identity is taken from the submitted form rather than the path, which security-principles.md flags under mass assignment and under trusting cross-request state
risks.mitigation: Identity comes from the path variable on every request. The controller's existing @InitBinder disallows id and *.id for every route it serves, so the new route inherits the control; the template's hidden petId field stays ignored in favor of the path variable

risks.risk: The reused form still reads as booking: the heading omits "New" for a persisted visit, and the button renders the addVisit key
risks.mitigation: Leave the template unchanged — reuse is the owner's recorded instruction, and the wording is a recorded PRD open question, not this slice's scope

notes: Verdict rationale: one small adjustment to an existing pattern suffices, so minor rather than covered (Pet gains a lookup and the model attribute gains a branch) and rather than new (no fresh design ground). Not conflicting: NG-5's narrowing is already recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-21-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md, and NG-4 is untouched — nothing is deleted. No new ADR: the reuse of an existing flow carries no hard-to-reverse trade-off, and the product decision already has its ADR. Narrowest readings recorded per the intake's standing instruction, since no further product answer will arrive: (a) no entry-point link is added anywhere; (b) a visit whose date has already passed cannot be corrected while keeping that date, which falls out of applying the booking rule unchanged (PRD Visits edge case 4) — no exemption is invented; (c) no confirmation message is added. Doc writes this dispatch: docs/system-design.md (four Contracts rows plus the invariant sentences) and docs/adr/README.md (the missing index row the prd-entry flagged). No design-doc-autofix records existed to audit. Pre-existing open questions this slice does not repair and does not widen: no service layer, and no modularity test.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Not run, not clean: no NVD match was performed for this review. The build declares no OWASP dependency-check plugin (build.gradle plugins: java, checkstyle, jacoco, spring-boot 4.1.0, dependency-management, graalvm native, cyclonedx, javaformat), and this reviewer has no network access. The change adds no dependency, so the supply-chain surface is unchanged from the last commit — but the Spring Boot 4.1.0 dependency set itself remains unverified against the NVD in this pipeline. The cyclonedx SBOM task exists; wiring an NVD match over it in CI would close the check permanently.

processVisitCorrectionForm takes @ModelAttribute Owner owner and calls owners.save(owner), so request parameters naming Owner fields (firstName, lastName, address, city, telephone, or nested pets[n].* properties) bind onto the persisted owner and are saved along with the correction. Identifier binding is blocked by the class-level @InitBinder, which is what docs/security-principles.md requires, and the construct is copied verbatim from the neighboring processNewVisitForm, so the change is not weaker than the recorded baseline — this is a recommendation, not a finding. If the pattern is ever tightened, tighten both handlers together: the correction handler needs no Owner form data at all and could take the owner from the model without rebinding (@ModelAttribute(binding = false)).

The correction handler binds request values directly onto the persistent Visit instance held in the owner's graph, before validation runs. It is safe here because spring.jpa.open-in-view=false leaves the graph detached outside the repository transaction and the failure path performs no save, so a rejected correction never reaches the database. That safety depends on the open-in-view setting; if it is ever flipped back to the Spring Boot default of true, the failure path would leave a dirty managed entity exposed to a flush by any later transactional call in the same request. Worth a comment at the setting rather than a code change now.
approved_aspects: Broken-object-level-authorization (IDOR) is closed by construction on the new correction routes: VisitController.loadPetWithVisit resolves the visit only through owner.getPet(petId).getVisit(visitId), so a visitId belonging to another owner or another pet of the same owner cannot be reached. Pet.getVisit scans only that pet's own collection and returns null otherwise, and the null branch throws rather than falling through to a fresh Visit. VisitControllerTests.theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitIsNotTheNamedPets pins the control.

Trusting-cross-request-state row of docs/security-principles.md is satisfied: both route pairs re-resolve owner, pet, and visit from the path on every request, the form carries no identifier, and the shared @InitBinder disallows 'id' and '*.id' so no identifier can be rebound from the request body onto the resolved graph.

The future-date rule is enforced on the correction path, not only on booking: rejectDateNotAfterToday is reached from both handlers, so a correction cannot move a visit into the past and an already-past visit cannot be resubmitted with its old date (theCorrectionOfAnAlreadyPastVisitShouldBeRefusedWhenItKeepsThatDate). Description remains bean-validated via @Valid.

No injection surface added: no string-concatenated query text, no shell or process execution, no file or resource path composed from request input, no deserialization entry point, no logging change. Data access stays on OwnerRepository derived queries.

XSS: the reused pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm template renders the prefilled description and date through th:field / th:text with Thymeleaf's default escaping on; no th:utext, no template-expression preprocessing, and no request-derived text reaches markup.

Error-disclosure: the new IllegalArgumentException message carries only the visitId and petId. visitId is typed Integer, so a non-numeric path segment fails conversion with a 400 before the message is composed, and error.html renders ${message} through escaped th:text. No credential, connection string, or internal detail is added to the error path.
No secrets introduced: a full-diff sweep for password/secret/token/key/credential returns nothing, and no configuration or credential file is touched.
Supply chain unchanged: build.gradle and the dependency set are outside this change set, so no new artifact or repository is introduced.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain, round 2: still not run, still not clean. The fix-delta (scripts/changeset.sh --base-tree 39a20dc) touches no build file and adds no artifact, so the supply-chain surface is unchanged from the round-1 basis — but the round-1 gap stands: the build declares no OWASP dependency-check plugin and this reviewer has no network access, so no NVD match was performed against the Spring Boot 4.1.0 dependency set in either round. A human or CI still owes this check; the existing cyclonedx SBOM task is the cheapest place to wire it.

Round-1 recommendations carried forward unchanged, because the code they describe is unchanged: (1) processVisitCorrectionForm takes @ModelAttribute Owner owner and saves it, so Owner-field request parameters ride along with a correction — blocked from identifier rebinding by the class-level @InitBinder and copied verbatim from processNewVisitForm, so no weaker than the recorded baseline; tighten both handlers together if ever tightened (@ModelAttribute(binding = false)). (2) The correction handler binds onto the persistent Visit before validation, safe only because spring.jpa.open-in-view=false detaches the graph and the failure path performs no save; a flip back to the Spring Boot default of true would expose a dirty managed entity on the rejection path. Worth a comment at the setting.
approved_aspects: No production delta since the reviewed basis. git diff 39a20dc..HEAD -- src/main/java/ is empty: VisitController.java and Pet.java are byte-identical to the tree I approved at line 19. The fix-delta is two docs prose edits (docs/adr/2026-08-21-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md line 13 'edit' to 'change'; docs/ubiquitous-language.md Visit/Correction entries) and two test files. Neither introduces a trust boundary, an input path, an output sink, a dependency, or a credential, so the round-1 threat-model walk over the correction routes still holds in full.

The new VisitControllerTests.theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenThePetIsNotTheNamedOwners closes the one IDOR rung round 1 asserted by reading code rather than by a pinned test: the pet-level check. Round 1 had theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitIsNotTheNamedPets pinning visit-under-pet; this pins pet-under-owner on the GET correction route, so both rungs of the owner-pet-visit resolution chain now fail closed under test. A regression that let owner.getPet(petId) fall through would now break the suite instead of silently widening object-level access.

PetTests.aVisitNotYetSavedShouldBeSkippedEvenWhenItsIdWouldMatch pins the security-relevant half of Pet.getVisit's guard. The production line (Pet.java:93) is !visit.isNew() && Objects.equals(visit.getId(), id): without the isNew() term, a null id would match any unsaved Visit in the collection and hand back a visit the caller never named. The path binding is a required Integer so no null reaches it today, but the test makes the guard load-bearing under change rather than incidental.

PetTests introduces no security surface of its own: pure in-memory value construction, no I/O, no temp files (nothing under /tmp or .scratch), no reflection, no randomness, no external fixture. Constants are non-sensitive domain literals ('Rabies booster', a relative LocalDate.now().plusDays(3)).
Secret sweep over the full fix-delta for password, secret, token, key, credential, passwd, apikey and auth returns nothing. No configuration, properties, or credential file is in the change set.

Docs delta is prose-only and security-neutral. The Correction entry records an in-place-change invariant and explicitly states that correcting a Visit never removes it and that the clinic does not cancel a booked Visit — vocabulary that narrows, never widens, the declined destructive operations. No route, permission, or data-handling claim is added or relaxed.

author: change-grader
summary: add a visit-correction route pair beside visit booking

blast_radius.note: Two production files in one module: VisitController gains a GET/POST route pair and a private date guard, Pet gains a 15-line lookup. No sensitive paths, no build or config files, no schema change; the remaining six files are docs prose recording the NG-5 narrowing.

semantic_surprise.note: Two behaviors the diff's surface does not advertise. processVisitCorrectionForm takes @ModelAttribute Owner owner and calls owners.save(owner), so request parameters naming Owner fields ride along with a visit correction and are persisted; identifiers are blocked by the class-level @InitBinder and the shape is copied verbatim from processNewVisitForm, but the correction route needs no Owner form data at all. Separately, the handler binds request values onto the persistent Visit already held in the owner's graph before validation runs, so the rejection path leaves a dirty in-memory entity, safe only because spring.jpa.open-in-view=false sits in application.properties, a file outside this diff. The extracted rejectDateNotAfterToday is behavior-identical; no operator or boundary was flipped.

test_adequacy.note: The tests assert real outcomes rather than restating the implementation: singleElement pins that a correction adds no second visit, verify(owners).save pins durability, both IDOR rungs (visit-under-pet and pet-under-owner) throw, and the already-past-visit boundary is covered. PetTests pins the isNew guard that would otherwise let a null id match an unsaved visit. One gap: no test asserts the rejection path performs no save, which is the control the pre-validation binding depends on.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four dispatched reviewers approved in round 2, but the security approval carries recommendations rather than none: the Owner mass-assignment ride-along and the open-in-view coupling are carried forward unchanged from round 1 as accepted-but-unresolved, and no NVD match was performed in either round because the build declares no dependency-check plugin and the reviewer has no network. Test and doc each requested changes in round 1 and were satisfied in round 2.

scope_deviation.note: The diff maps onto REQ-VISITEDIT-001 and stops where the requirement stops: no owner-record link, no cancellation, no lifecycle state. The NG-5 narrowing that authorizes it is the human's own intake decision, quoted verbatim in the new ADR. One design revision and one design-mismatch build abort along the way, both resolved before the passing build; no consultations, no build retries.

rationale: Correct and contained, but read the correction POST before merging: it binds and saves the whole Owner from request parameters, and its rejection path is safe only because spring.jpa.open-in-view=false lives outside this diff. Security approved both as carried-forward recommendations, and no test pins the no-save-on-rejection control.
